payload.problem_domain: Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook chapter review and disposition

payload.statement:
Chapter under review: ch17 (quarto-book/chapters/17-magic-items.qmd), "Magic Items", 413 lines.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files a finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope

Findings cite [file:line] in the chapter (17-magic-items.qmd). Mechanics
findings state the broken value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks
use the authoritative chapters as the reference, not this chapter (core
rules = ch06: DR math, minimum-1 damage, one-roll principle; combat = ch13:
Damage Types, Conditions table (Table 13.3), Shared Effects, Defense Roll,
Morale Check; social = ch14: the attitude ladder (Hostile, Neutral, Friendly,
Allied) and how attitude shifts work; disciplines = ch08: the Discipline
Taxonomy (23 disciplines, 9 categories) and tier/prereq shapes; equipment =
ch15: pricing and kit lines; bestiary = ch20: monster stat blocks; glossary =
ch21; reference sheets = ch22).

Disposition classes (for the librarian's synthesis):
  mechanical    - safe to implement as a micro-PR (headings, tables, wording,
                  em-dashes, single-cell refs, budget rows, worked-example
                  arithmetic that is canon-determined by another chapter)
  substantive   - needs a dispatched implementation pass (multi-file, new
                  content, worked-example rewrite requiring new narrative)
  design-decision - needs Bruce's ruling; implement the recommended default,
                  flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md

Standing book conventions are in force: zero em-dashes in book text; damage
budgets flat at Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21; card costs 2/4/8;
Adept prereqs exactly 2, Master exactly 3; no flat +N damage riders anywhere
in the book (a damage bonus must be a budget row, a Basic-card floor of
1/2/3 + attribute, or a "+1 damage tier" bump); one-roll principle (the hit
or casting roll IS the outcome, no second damage roll); leveled conditions
(Burning X, Frozen X, Slowed X) carry their number in the condition name and
card text; Boon/Bane and the -2/-1 modifier ladder are the only numeric
roll modifiers (a flat "-1 to attack rolls" in an effect is NOT a canonical
modifier form); attributes run -2 to +2 and no rule may require a +3
attribute score or modifier. Violations of these conventions are findings,
not questions.

Known context for the council (verify, don't trust the summary): the chapter
is 413 lines with 25 item entries (lines 41-372), an Attunement section
(373-388), a Discipline Items table (389-403), and Finding Magic Items
(404-413). Two items repeat the same granted effect: Cloak of Elvenkind
(lines 57-63) and Veilwalker's Shroud (lines 65-79) both grant Boon on
Stealth checks. The chapter cites [file:line] references to other chapters
(@sec-chapter-damage-budget, @sec-chapter-equipment) whose anchors must
resolve. Item damage rows must land flat on a budget row (e.g. an item keyed
to the Novice row uses 2/4/6; a potion's Greater tier uses 6/9/12, Superior
9/15/21). Consumable "spend an action" healing and "once per day/encounter"
limits are canonical item design. The chapter also contains a Discipline
Items table granting disciplines to non-magic users; verify each discipline
name appears in the ch08 taxonomy exactly as spelled.

Scope note: the chapter is the canonical home for magic item rules. Where
another chapter contradicts it, the finding should name BOTH files and
identify which is canonical (ch17 for item rules; ch13/ch14/ch08 for the
mechanics it references). Figure-caption doubling (the "Illo 24: Magic Items
Art" image alt text + the italic caption line) is a BOOK-WIDE convention
already routed to decisions-pending as #36 — do NOT raise it as a per-chapter
finding; a chapter-local fix would make this chapter inconsistent with the
book. The council's output is a disposition plan; it does not itself edit
the book.

payload.argument: The item-card skeleton holds on this lens: activated powers resolve on one roll, rows are Weak/Standard/Strong, and most numbers are flat on a canonical budget row. Compliant audit pass: Rare one-discipline items key the Novice row 2/4/6 (Blade of the Last Ember rows at 17:53-55, Stormcaller's Gauntlets 17:93-95, Frost Brand 17:207-209, Elixir of Dragon's Breath 17:355-357); Very Rare items key the Adept row 6/9/12 (Mantle of the Burning Shield 17:171-173, Thunder Maul 17:223-225); Potion of Healing sits on 2/4/6 and its Greater and Superior variants sit exactly on the Adept and Master rows (17:339-343); Horn of the Dawn's Strong radiant line is a flat on-row value (17:133); every +1 damage tier bump (17:47, 201, 217, 233, 257, 272) is the one permitted rider; no damage dice appear anywhere. Five mechanics defects require changes, each with the broken value and expected value. (1) Sunbow (17:255-257): the damage rows read 0/2/6; the Standard row carries 2, the Novice Weak value, where the item's Rare/1-Fire keying requires the row value 4, and the Weak row names Dazzled while applying a flat minus-one attack penalty, whereas the conditions table defines Dazzled as a sight-based Perception Bane with no attack-roll component (13:175); expected is the full Novice row 2/4/6 with the canonical Dazzled (or a Bane). (2) Chalice of Shared Mercy (17:107-109): every tier repeats the same 2 HP entry, so the self-heal never scales; the card reaches the Novice totals 2/4/6 only if the reader sums recipients, a reading the text never states; expected is a scaling 2/4/6 self-heal, or an explicit statement that row totals key to the budget (wording fix; design ruling only if the split is intended). (3) Titan's Girdle (17:117): a Brawn score of +3 exceeds the attribute ceiling of -2 to +2 (03:41-45); expected is the +2 maximum or a Boon on Brawn checks for lifting and breaking. (4) Immovable Rod (17:325): the check band Strong 17-20 does not exist; Strong is 15-18+ (06:29-31), and the chapter's own Rope of Climbing entry uses the correct Standard 9-14 (17:305); expected is Strong 15-18+. (5) Locket of the Final Word (17:183): the promised two-step shift toward Friendly is contradicted by its own Hostile example, which moves only one step to Neutral; per the ch14 ladder (14:39-44) two steps from Hostile lands on Friendly, while the Neutral example's two steps land on Allied, so no single step count satisfies all three statements; expected is one consistent rule: either two steps (Hostile to Friendly, Neutral to Allied) or one step (Hostile to Neutral, Neutral to Friendly). Two smaller defects: the Discipline Items prose grants a Blade Discipline where the taxonomy and the chapter's own table both spell the discipline Blades (08:37, 17:391, 17:399); and the Finding Magic Items pacing rule reserves Weak/Standard/Strong items for levels 7-10 while the same chapter issues Weak/Standard/Strong Potions of Healing at levels 1-3 (17:408-410), so that clause must be dropped or scoped to Rare-and-above items. All fixes are single-cell or single-clause wording changes (mechanical), except the Chalice split-heal intent (design-decision with a mechanical default).

The Finding Magic Items guidance reserves Weak/Standard/Strong items for levels 7-10 while the same chapter issues Weak/Standard/Strong Potions of Healing at levels 1-3 [17-magic-items:408-410, 339-341].

payload.argument:
Structural claims in the brief all verify. The chapter has exactly 25 item entries (17-magic-items.qmd:41-370; headings at 41, 57, 65, 81, 97, 111, 121, 135, 149, 159, 175, 187, 195, 211, 227, 243, 259, 275, 285, 295, 309, 319, 329, 345, 361), followed by Attunement (373-388), Discipline Items (389-403), and Finding Magic Items (404-413). Both cross-references resolve: the damage-budget anchor points at the Damage Budget section in 08-disciplines.qmd:172, and the talents/abilities anchor points at 09-talents-abilities.qmd:1; the chapter never cites an equipment anchor, so nothing dangles there. No em-dashes occur in the chapter (grep: zero hits). All seven discipline names in the Discipline Items table appear verbatim in the ch08 taxonomy (08-disciplines.qmd:33-55), and the prose shorthand 'Blade Discipline' (17:391) mirrors ch08's own prose usage (08:23). Condition naming otherwise tracks Table 13.3: numbered leveled conditions carry their numbers (Burning 2 at 55 and 357, Slowed 5 at 208, Frozen 2 at 209), and plain conditions are plain (Blinded at 54-55, Prone at 207, Stunned at 95 and 225, Invisible at 79 and 241). Potion rows land flat on budget rows (2/4/6 at 339-341; 6/9/12 and 9/15/21 at 343), as do the other damage rows (2/4/6 at 53-55, 93-95; 6/9/12 at 171-173, 223-225). Armor/shield figures agree with ch15 (plate DR 6 at 15-equipment.qmd:89; shield +2 DR at 15-equipment.qmd:93).

However, five canon-contradicting values fail verification:

1. Sunbow's Blinding Volley rows (255-257) are no damage on Weak, 2 on Standard, 6 on Strong; no flat budget row has that shape. The budget table (08-disciplines.qmd:176-180; 21-glossary.qmd:43) defines exactly three rows: 2/4/6, 6/9/12, 9/15/21. Expected: the Novice row 2/4/6 for this Rare item, or an explicit off-row justification.

2. Immovable Rod (325) brackets the check to force the rod with '(Strong 17-20)', but Table 6.1 (06-core-resolution.qmd:29-31) puts Strong at 15-18+. A 15 or 16 is Strong by the core rules yet below the rod's bracket. Expected: '(Strong 15+)'.

3. Sunbow's Dazzled (255) imposes a flat -1 on attack rolls, which is not what the Conditions Table defines Dazzled to be: Table 13.3 (13-combat.qmd:175) says Perception checks at Bane and no Boon on sight-based rolls. The effect redefines a canonical condition, and a flat numeric penalty in an effect is not a canonical modifier form (Boon/Bane are the sanctioned roll modifiers, 06-core-resolution.qmd:43-47). Expected: the canonical Dazzled effect, or a differently named mechanic.

4. Titan's Girdle (117) treats Brawn as +3 for carrying, lifting, and breaking, but attribute scores are capped at +2 and the book forbids anything above (03-attributes.qmd:30, 52; the score table at 32-38 tops at +2). Expected: at most +2, or restate as Boon on the relevant Brawn checks.

5. Locket of the Final Word (183) grants a two-step attitude shift toward Friendly but its own example moves Hostile to Neutral, which is one step on the ch14 ladder (14-social-conflict.qmd:39-44: Hostile, Neutral, Friendly, Allied). The Neutral-to-Allied example is correctly two steps, so the Hostile case is the error. Expected: Hostile becomes Friendly under a two-step rule, or the rule says one step.

Minor: Horn of the Dawn's Weak row (131) wraps the condition as 'the Frightened condition' while its Standard and Strong rows (132-133) use the plain name; card-text convention elsewhere uses plain names (13-combat.qmd:211). Align line 131. The Cloak of Elvenkind / Veilwalker's Shroud duplication (63 and 71) is verified fact: word-identical passives, both Uncommon, both Cloak type, both attunement-required. It is a genuine mechanical redundancy for the Author lens to resolve (merge, differentiate, or rename one).

Verdict: on the factual-verification lens the chapter does not hold as written. Four mechanical fixes are canon-determined (Sunbow row, Rod bracket, Girdle cap, Locket step count), Dazzled needs a condition-definition alignment, plus one wording nit and one duplication for the author. Everything else the brief asked to verify holds.

payload.argument:
Verdict: refute. The chapter does not survive devil's-advocate stress-testing as written; each item below names a concrete counter-example and a fix with its scope.

1) One-roll principle broken by target saves. The combat chapter says effects ride the attack or casting roll, never a second roll, and flatly adds 'No check' [13-combat:146]. Six items here impose target checks as second rolls: Blade of the Last Ember [17-magic-items:54], Stormcaller's Gauntlets [17-magic-items:94], Frost Brand [17-magic-items:207-208], Thunder Maul [17-magic-items:224], Sunbow [17-magic-items:251,256], and Elixir of Dragon's Breath [17-magic-items:356-357]. The combat chapter defines no Fortitude or Agility save mechanic; its only defender-side rolls are the Defense Roll and the Morale Check, and the wound-table Fortitude check is a hardship roll, not a defense [13-combat:314]. The chapter's own parentheticals marking rows as '(no check)' [17-magic-items:55,257] prove check-based resolution is its default, so the two subsystems coexist with no bridging rule. Broken value: second target rolls in six items. Expected value: either ch13 gains a saves rule that ch17 references, or riders convert to tier-keyed effects per [13-combat:146]. Counter-example: one item, Blade of the Last Ember, resolves its Blind rider via a Fortitude check on Standard and by flat application on Strong [17-magic-items:54-55]; the choice of subsystem is per-row whim, not a defined mechanic.

2) Locket of the Final Word arithmetic contradicts itself. The rule states a two-step shift toward Friendly, then gives examples: a Hostile target becomes Neutral (one step) and a Neutral target becomes Allied (two steps, past Friendly) [17-magic-items:183]. On the four-rung ladder of the social chapter (Hostile, Neutral, Friendly, Allied) [14-social-conflict:41-44], two steps up from Hostile lands on Friendly, not Neutral, and 'toward Friendly' misdescribes a landing at Allied. The once-per-campaign cost and crumbling-to-dust [17-magic-items:185] do cap the charm-every-NPC worry, so a no-save effect at that price is defensible; the broken text is the step arithmetic. Expected: Hostile to Friendly under the two-step reading, or a one-step rule with Neutral to Friendly.

3) Immovable Rod check band is off-book. Forcing the rod requires a Brawn check at 'Strong 17-20' [17-magic-items:325]. The canonical Strong band is 15+ [21-glossary:35; 22-reference-sheets:25], every other Strong DC in the book is 'Strong 15+' (e.g., manacles [15-equipment:134]), and 3d6 cannot exceed 18, so 19-20 are unrollable. Expected: 'Strong 15+'.

4) Bag and rod: the classic combo is preempted, with two residual holes. The rod-in-bag exploit is explicitly forbidden with a stated consequence (interior piercing destroys the bag and scatters its contents) [17-magic-items:293], and the bag's 'items' wording [17-magic-items:291] excludes creatures, closing the stuff-a-creature trick. No counter-example found there. Residual holes: (a) bag-in-bag is warned against but no consequence is given for it [17-magic-items:293], undefined behavior for the one action the text singles out; (b) the rod's 8,000-lb static rating [17-magic-items:325] has no stated behavior under a falling load or creature, leaving a save-free feather-fall trick to DA whim. The 500-lb vs 8,000-lb figures are not contradictory; they are different capacities for different objects.

5) Rope of Climbing is an at-will grapple. The rope can be aimed at any point within 60 ft and fastens itself there [17-magic-items:301], with no inanimate-object restriction, no roll, no save, and no daily limit. A creature is a point. The willingness restriction appears only in the Strong harness row [17-magic-items:307], proving the base power does not require it. Counter-example: designate an enemy as the destination; the rope wraps and holds them at will, bypassing the opposed grappling roll of the combat chapter [13-combat:207]. Expected: restrict destinations to inanimate points, or require a check or save to bind a creature.

6) Sunbow misuses a named condition. Its Weak row applies Dazzled as a -1 attack penalty [17-magic-items:255], but the combat chapter defines Dazzled as a perception-affecting condition (Bane on perception checks, no Boon on sight-based rolls) [13-combat:175]. Same name, different effect; and the flat numeric attack penalty is a modifier form the book's standing conventions reject (only Boon/Bane and the -2/-1 ladder may modify rolls). Expected: use the canonical Dazzled effect, or switch the rider to Blinded.

7) Titan's Girdle breaks the attribute ceiling. It treats Brawn as +3 for carrying, lifting, and breaking [17-magic-items:117]; the attributes chapter caps every attribute at +2 and calls the narrow range intentional [03-attributes:45,52]. Applied to breaking objects, the +3 also acts as a roll bonus of a magnitude the modifier system does not contain. Expected: +2 with a different rider (e.g., Boon on lifting checks), or an explicit ruling that the item is a deliberate exception.

8) 'Artifact' is undefined. The attunement section exempts Artifacts from the three-slot cap [17-magic-items:375], yet the chapter's rarity list tops out at Legendary [17-magic-items:24] and the only other occurrence in the book merely repeats the clause [21-glossary:179]. Nothing defines what an Artifact is, so the clause is either dead text or an open door for any DA to bypass the cap the chapter itself calls load-bearing [17-magic-items:380]. Expected: define Artifact as the tier above Legendary, or delete the clause.

9) Deck of Many Things is the only activated item with no frequency limit. Every other activated item states once per encounter, day, session, or campaign; the deck just says 'Draw a Card' [17-magic-items:193], its size is fluid [17-magic-items:191], fates are DA-decided with no roll to resist, and it needs no attunement. Counter-example: the whole party draws repeatedly in one sitting, each draw a campaign-ending whim with no stated cap. Expected: a stated limit (once per session or per character) or a fixed deck of defined fates.

10) Spellguard mixes cooldown units. Spell Catch is once per encounter [17-magic-items:267], but a Weak result disables it for the rest of the session [17-magic-items:271]; two frequency units in one item, with the roughly one-in-four Weak outcome on 3d6 costing the signature reaction for a whole session. Expected: aligned units.

11) Strict dominance: Cloak of Elvenkind vs Veilwalker's Shroud. Same rarity, same attunement, identical Stealth Boon passive [17-magic-items:63,71]; the Shroud adds a once-per-encounter teleport [17-magic-items:73-79]. The Cloak is strictly worse, so no player ever chooses it. Expected: differentiate the Cloak or drop it.

12) Temporary disciplines vs permanent purchases. Item-granted ranks count toward prereqs and unlock Adept and Master abilities like purchased ones [17-magic-items:391], but the disciplines chapter frames mastery as permanent with no expiration [08-disciplines:15] and gates item-granted disciplines to Rare items [08-disciplines:91] while the table here grants them from Uncommon items [17-magic-items:395-398]. Two edges: unattuning strands purchased abilities whose prereqs were item-sourced (no rule covers it), and the rarity gate disagrees. Expected: a rule for lost item-sourced prereqs and a reconciled rarity gate.

13) Tested, no counter-example found: Horn of the Dawn [17-magic-items:133] - its 6-radiant burst against undead (skeleton HP 5 [20-bestiary:124]) can trigger the combat chapter's morale trigger for half the group fallen [13-combat:269], but that cascade is DA-called, once per day, and needs a Strong roll; coherent. Chalice of Shared Mercy [17-magic-items:107-109] - the 2/4/6 spread matches the healing rows of the potions [17-magic-items:339-343]; sharing is a tax, not a loophole, total throughput never beats the single-target rows. Mirror of Echoing Eyes [17-magic-items:141-147] - once per session holds; the undetectable Strong tier is a surveillance weapon, with a minor recommendation for same-plane or alive guardrails. Attunement cap [17-magic-items:375] is otherwise fine; every discipline name used here matches the ch08 taxonomy (Fire, Earth, Wind, Water, Blades, Religion, Animal, Life).

payload.argument:
Voice verdict first: the chapter reads like the rest of the book. All 25 entries carry vivid narrative flavor and never degrade into stat-block soup; the wry asides (the playtesters jab in the Immovable Rod entry, the two-word closing nudge of Finding Magic Items) sit comfortably next to the established register seen in the front matter's thanks and the ancestry chapter's dry one-liners. The Attunement callout [17:373-385] and the Finding Magic Items callout [17:403-413] speak in the same plain, direct address as the surrounding book. On flavor and tone the chapter holds. Consistency does not hold, in five places with named fixes:

1. Twin stealth cloaks. Cloak of Elvenkind [17:57-63] and Veilwalker's Shroud [17:65-79] are the same rarity, same slot type, same attunement requirement, and carry a word-for-word identical passive granting a Stealth-check boon [17:63, 17:71]; their flavor lines are near-mirrors (forest forgetting the wearer versus world forgetting the wearer) [17:61, 17:69]. The Shroud's teleport maneuver differentiates the mechanics, but a reader who meets the second item eleven lines after the first experiences the same card twice, and both items use a 'gain' construction where the chapter's three other boon passives and the rest of the book use a 'have' construction [17:119, 17:265, 17:369; 04:190], which deepens the twin feel. Fix: give the Cloak a distinct granted effect (e.g., scope its stealth boon to natural surroundings) so no verbatim overlap remains; this needs a design ruling on the replacement effect.

2. Condition-name collision on Dazzled. The Sunbow's blinding volley labels its effect with the Dazzled condition name while glossing it as an attack penalty [17:255], but the canonical Dazzled condition in the combat chapter is a perception-bane state with no attack-penalty meaning at all [13-combat:175]. One condition name carrying two different mechanical meanings is precisely the collision this lens hunts for, and the glossed penalty form also sits outside the book's approved modifier vocabulary. Fix: rename the Sunbow's effect (the chapter already uses the Blinded condition elsewhere) or restate it in canonical Dazzled terms; substantive wording fix.

3. Condition-phrasing outlier. The Horn of the Dawn's weak row is the only place in the entire book that wraps a condition name in a definite-article construction [17:131]; the very next row of the same table drops the wrapper [17:132], and the combat chapter names conditions bare [13-combat:171-187]. Fix: strip the wrapper so both rows read the same way; mechanical micro-edit.

4. Repeating thesis phrases. The intro makes three signature claims and the section lead under the items heading restates each of them within forty lines: the no-generic-sword claim appears twice [17:13, 17:23], the named-and-unique claim twice [17:23, 17:39], the found-not-bought claim twice [17:13, 17:39]. The lead should advance the section, not echo the intro. Fix: vary or cut one copy of each; mechanical micro-edit.

5. Taxonomy-name ambiguity in the Discipline Items prose. The prose grants a discipline in the singular-adjective form [17:391] while the chapter's own table lists the grant under the taxonomy plural form [17:399], and the disciplines chapter defines a category with the plural spelling while a distinct discipline is literally named with the singular spelling [08:37, 08:74]. The prose form can therefore be misread as granting the wrong thing. Fix: align the prose with the taxonomy plural spelling; mechanical micro-edit.

Minor note: the Locket's campaign-frequency phrase [17:181] appears nowhere else in the book (the established frequencies are per session, per day, per encounter, at will), and the entry's own destruction line already encodes the once-ever limit, so the novel phrase is redundant flavor. Acceptable as design, but worth a glossary nod or a simpler phrase.

FRAMING: As librarian I weigh the chapter against the book's own standing conventions and the brief's disposition classes, then preview the plan shape. Ledger check: positions are empty, so I am weighing the chapter cold; no other member's stance exists to reconcile yet.

(1) PUBLISHABLE-UNIT ASSESSMENT: The chapter has a coherent publishable skeleton: a reading guide (lines 19-27), 25 uniform cards (41-370), Attunement (373-385), a Discipline Items table (389-401), and a DA-facing Finding Magic Items callout (403-413). Convention compliance is largely real, not claimed: zero em-dashes (grep count 0); one-roll phrasing throughout (26, 335); leveled conditions carry their number (Burning 2 at 55 and 357, Slowed 5 at 208, Frozen 2 at 209); Boon/Bane is the only roll modifier except one violation noted below (63, 71, 119, 132-133, 240, 265, 369); damage rows land flat on 2/4/6 (53-55, 93-95, 339-341, 355-357), 6/9/12 (171-173, 223-225), and 9/15/21 (343); the '+1 damage tier' bump is the only damage rider form used (47, 201, 217, 233, 257, 272) - no flat +N riders anywhere. But it does NOT hold as written: four defects are must-fix.

(2) MY OWN AUDIT OBSERVATIONS (voting member, independent of other roles):
  (a) Locket of the Final Word is internally contradictory [181-185]: the blanket 'two steps' rule cannot coexist with the worked examples. On the four-rung ch14 ladder, Hostile to Neutral is one step and Neutral to Allied is two, so no single step count matches both examples and the general sentence. Broken value: general rule plus examples disagree. Expected value: self-consistent ladder math (canon-determined by ch14); recommended default: 'two steps toward Allied, a Hostile creature becomes Friendly' or keep both examples by special-casing Hostile to one step. This is the chapter's clearest factual error.
  (b) Sunbow's rows [253-257] are 0/2/6 - the Weak tier deals no damage and Standard deals 2, skipping the Novice 2/4/6 row's middle rung. The chapter's own rule at line 27 keys damaging powers to the flat budget, so this is a mechanics finding: broken value 0/2/6, expected 2/4/6 (with Dazzled folded into a tier) unless the control-trade is an intentional design exception.
  (c) The reading guide [23-26] glosses only Name, Rarity, Attunement, and Granted Action, but every weapon entry also carries Type and Disciplines tags (e.g. 43, 83, 99, 161, 197, 213, 245) that are never explained. A reader cannot parse a full card from the guide. Mechanical: add Type and Disciplines bullets.
  (d) Sunbow Weak [255] uses a raw '-1 to attack rolls' parenthetical, which is not a canonical modifier form per the standing conventions (Boon/Bane and the -2/-1 ladder are the only numeric roll modifiers). If Dazzled is not a defined condition in ch13's Table 13.3, this is substantive (a condition-table addition); if it is, it is a mechanical wording fix.
  (e) Titan's Girdle [117] treats Brawn as +3 for carrying, lifting, and breaking. It does not require a +3 score and explicitly excludes attack and damage rolls, so it may not violate the -2 to +2 ceiling, but any +3 anywhere in the book deserves Bruce's ruling. Design-decision; recommended default: keep as scoped.
  (f) 'Artifacts do not count against this limit' [375] references a category that appears nowhere in the chapter's rarity ladder [24] and, from this source, nowhere in the book. Verify book-wide; if undefined, either define it in ch17 (mechanical) or route to glossary (substantive).
  (g) Cloak of Elvenkind [57-63] and Veilwalker's Shroud [65-79] share an identical passive at identical rarity and attunement, but the Shroud also grants Step Between, so the Cloak is strictly dominated - a balance smell, not just an echo. Design-decision; recommended default: differentiate the Cloak's passive.
  (h) Chalice of Shared Mercy [103-109] heals a flat 2 HP on every tier while the potions [339-343] scale on budget rows. Line 27 binds only 'damaging powers', so this is not a mechanics violation; the spread-not-scale contrast is plausibly intentional. Design-decision, low severity; default: keep.
  (i) The brief's known-context list names anchors (@sec-chapter-damage-budget, @sec-chapter-equipment) that do not exist in the source; the chapter's actual cross-references are @sec-chapter-talents-abilities [21] and @sec-damage-budget [27]. Anchor resolution is a mechanical verify-only item against the book.
  (j) 'Once per session' [141] and 'once per campaign' [181] extend the canonical day/encounter limit family to narrative cadences. Acceptable in spirit; note for the ledger rather than a finding.
  (k) Verify-only cross-chapter items (cannot be resolved from this source): shield '+2 DR' [265] and 'Plate is normally 6' [281] against ch15; DC-band forms 'Standard 9-14' [305] and 'Strong 17-20' [325] against ch06; 'swimming Speed' [367] and oil-flask economics [317]; discipline spellings against the ch08 taxonomy, especially plural 'Blades' [399] and 'Religion' [400].
  (l) Excluded per scope note: figure-caption doubling [7-9, 31-33] is book-wide decision #36, not raised here.

(3) DISPOSITION PLAN SHAPE PREVIEW: mechanical (micro-PR): (a) Locket step-count rewrite, (b) Sunbow row flatten, (c) reading-guide Type/Disciplines bullets, (d) Dazzled wording fix, (i) anchor verification, discipline-spelling check, DC-band and DR cross-ref verification, comma-splice cleanup at 391. Substantive (dispatched pass): only if Dazzled is absent from ch13's conditions or Artifacts is undefined book-wide (both multi-file). Design-decision (decisions-pending.md, implemented defaults, veto-revertible): (e) Girdle +3 keep-as-scoped, (f) Artifacts define in ch17, (g) differentiate Cloak of Elvenkind, (h) Chalice flat healing keep, session/campaign cadence accept. Net: the chapter is close to publishable; the change set is small and mostly mechanical, but the Locket contradiction and Sunbow row are hard blockers as written.

No check') - f-003's flagship finding, un-rebutted; (6) 'Artifacts' is referenced in the attunement cap (17:375) and the glossary (21:179) but never defined anywhere - f-003/f-005/f-007; (7) Cloak of Elvenkind is strictly dominated by Veilwalker's Shroud (identical passive at identical rarity/attunement; Shroud adds a maneuver) - f-003/f-004/f-007; (8) the Finding Magic Items guidance (17:410) withholds W/S/S items until levels 7-10 while the same chapter issues W/S/S potions at levels 1-3 - f-001/f-005; (9) the reading guide glosses four fields but cards carry unexplained Type and Disciplines tags - f-005/f-007; (10) the Discipline Items prose grants '1 Blade Discipline' against the taxonomy's 'Blades' plural - f-001/f-004, and ch08's 'Rare magic items may grant... permanent Disciplines' conflicts with ch17's Uncommon temporary discipline items - f-003. The layout-expert's support is scoped strictly to presentation (headings, tables, pagebreaks, em-dash law all clean) and does not rebut the mechanics defects; the chapter is not publishable as written. payload.recommendation: Chapter 17 (Magic Items) is REJECTED as a publishable unit on mechanics and consistency: the Locket's attitude-shift arithmetic is self-contradictory, the Sunbow's damage rows are off-budget and it hijacks the Dazzled condition name with a non-canonical -1 attack penalty, the Immovable Rod uses a nonexistent check band, the Titan's Girdle exceeds the attribute ceiling, six items violate the locked one-roll principle with Fortitude/Agility target checks, 'Artifact' is referenced but undefined, two Uncommon cloaks are functionally identical (strict dominance), the level-band guidance contradicts the chapter's own potions, and the reading guide omits the Type and Disciplines card fields. The presentation layer is clean. Fix per disposition plan: one mechanical micro-PR implementing (a) Locket step-count rewrite to match its examples, (b) Sunbow rows flattened to the Novice 2/4/6 budget with canonical Dazzled (Perception Bane, no attack penalty), (c) Immovable Rod band corrected to Strong 15+, (d) Titan's Girdle converted to a Boon on Brawn checks (ceiling law), (e) item target-check riders converted to tier-keyed effects per the one-roll principle (Blade, Gauntlets, Frost Brand, Thunder Maul, Sunbow, Elixir - six cards), (f) Artifact defined as the tier above Legendary in both ch17 and ch21, (g) Cloak of Elvenkind differentiated (Stealth Boon scoped to natural surroundings) with the 'gain Boon' passive convention aligned to 'have Boon', (h) Finding Magic Items W/S/S clause deleted, (i) reading-guide Type/Disciplines bullets added, (j) '1 Blade Discipline' aligned to the taxonomy plural, (k) Rope of Climbing restricted to inanimate destinations, (l) Deck of Many Things given a once-per-session limit, (m) Spellguard cooldown units aligned to once-per-encounter, (n) bag-in-bag consequence stated, (o) Discipline Items lost-prereq rule added and ch08's rarity/permanence gate reconciled, (p) intro/lead repetition trimmed, (q) Horn of the Dawn condition-phrasing outlier aligned.
